Hi Anna,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, I put together a short checklist of operator-level evidence items Medigroup asked for around EU-only processing, retention, and deletion. Before I share the checklist with Legal, quick questions so we can make the artifacts as targeted as possible: 

- Do you need live request-level traces (per-request headers + region routing) or are aggregated routing logs sufficient?
- For backups: should we provide proof of backup location + retention windows, or do you need proof of destruction for backups when a deletion request is made?
- On bridge letters / mitigating measures under SCCs: is a short attestation from Redwood about non-US access plus our HSM/KMS controls enough, or will you need tenant-level key custody evidence?

I've attached an internal draft checklist and a suggested bridge-letter template (short). Happy to iterate. If it's helpful, we can do a 30-minute run-through with your security team next week.

From: Anna Lemoine <anna.lemoine@medigroup.eu>

Hi Soojin,

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side to make sure we request the right things from Redwood Legal/Security: 

- Routing logs: aggregated routing + a short sample of request-level traces (anonymized IDs) is what our security reviewers usually accept. So the routing log summary plus 10 anonymized traces per week is our ask.
- Backups: we need proof of location and the documented retention policy. For deletions, an operational description of the backup restore window and the timeline for purging deleted tenant data is fine; we do not require per-deletion forensic certification for every request, but we may ask for an attestation for our SLA/contract.
- Bridge letters: a short operator attestation that details (1) no routine access from non-EU jurisdictions, (2) KMS controls and who holds keys, and (3) audit log retention/availability — that typically satisfies our legal team; they reserve the right to ask for tenant-level key custody in high-risk cases.

We'd like a consolidated "operator checklist" that maps each item to an artifact (log export, policy doc, screenshot, DSAR playbook). Can we get that by end of week? If not, propose a date and we'll schedule a short sync.

Regards,
Anna
Security Programs Manager, Medigroup

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Hi Anna — apologies for the delayed consolidation. Attaching the operator checklist (redwood-eu-ops-checklist-v1.xlsx) and a short draft bridge-letter (sccs-bridge-letter-draft.docx). High-level answers below and next steps: 

- Routing trace samples: exported 10 anonymized traces and an hourly routing summary CSV (link in Drive). Samples include hashed request_id, ingress region, model_version, and serving_region.
- Backups & retention: primary backups for tenant config and state are stored in eu-west-1 with lifecycle policy: hot backups 30 days, archived snapshots 90 days, and encrypted-at-rest using KMS keys whose root is in EU KMS. For DSAR deletion, we mark tenant objects for deletion immediately; background job purges backups on the next snapshot cycle — documented ~90 day worst-case for snapshot lifecycle. We included the policy doc excerpt in the checklist.
- Deletion evidence: we can provide a log extract showing the deletion marker timestamp, snapshot ID, and subsequent snapshot purge (where applicable). This is the artifact we map in the checklist.
- Bridge-letter: the draft attests to (1) EU-only processing for data-plane, (2) KMS ownership/confines to EU region, (3) emergency access controls and audit logging. If Medigroup requires tenant-level key custody we can discuss options (BYOK roadmap).

Next steps: Please confirm if the artifacts meet your legal team's needs. If yes, I'll upload the sanitized logs and the CSVs to the Drive link and share a DocuSign-ready bridge-letter. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call next week to walk through.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Principal Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
